4.3.11 Transport and Value Error Counters Handling
The Error Counters are introduced in order to give the software components extra
information about the errors occurred during the signal and signal group processing.
This extra information is added as optional parameter to the RTE Read API Rte_Read.
There is two types of error counters:
• The transport protocol errors incremented when data is not received due to one
of the following errors occur since last RTE cyclic reception:
– Com error (e.g. Com deadline monitoring)
• The data value errors when the value received have to one of the following errors
occur since the last call of the respective RTE API:
– Out of range value error
– Invalid value error
[SWS_Rte_04666] Storage of Communication Transport Errors Count ⌈The RTE
shall store number of transport protocol errors counter (errors due to no data is received
by COM) if the transportErrorCountEnabled for the port mapped to the signal
is set to TRUE. This counter (TransportErrorCount) shall be returned as part of
optional parameter Rte_ComErrorInfo that can be returned from Rte API Calls.⌋
[SWS_Rte_04667] Incrementing Transport Error Counters ⌈If no data is received
by COM within full read process cycle within Rte cyclic function for respective signal
or signal group, then the RTE shall increment the transport protocol errors counter (
TransportErrorCount).⌋
[SWS_Rte_04668] Resetting Transport Error Counters ⌈If a full read process cycle
within Rte cyclic function for respective signal or signal group has been passed suc-
cessfully without any error, the RTE shall reset the transport protocol errors counter (
TransportErrorCount).⌋
[SWS_Rte_04669] Transport Error Counters Maximum Value ⌈If the transport pro-
tocol errors counter (TransportErrorCount) value already is maximum value (255),
then the counter value shall not be increased any more but stay at maximum value(255)
if further errors are encountered.⌋
